skills.short: Builds a whole site end to end and owns AWARDS.md; the entry point when you are unsure which skill applies.
skills.title: the orchestrating skill
skills.description: Design and build award-worthy websites end to end (Site of the Day and Developer Award league): brief → concept → system → structure → stack → motion → WebGL → jury → ship. Use when the user wants a site, landing page, portfolio, campaign, product or studio site that should be 'award-worthy', 'award-level', 'immersive', 'cinematic', 'creative-developer style', with smooth scroll, GSAP or WebGL, names studios or award sites (Lusion, Igloo, Lando Norris), or says 'make it stunning'. The entry point when unsure which awards skill applies; owns AWARDS.md. Not for dashboards, admin CRUD, bug fixes, API docs or accessibility work without award framing.
skills.lead: Design and build award-worthy websites end to end (Site of the Day and Developer Award league): brief → concept → system → structure → stack → motion → WebGL → jury → ship.
skills.intro: This skill turns a brief into a finished, judged and shipped site by driving the other awards skills in order. It never does their work itself: it captures the brief, keeps `AWARDS.md` honest, routes each phase to the right skill, calibrates against the award rubric and refuses to call a build finished before a jury and a ship report exist.
skills.hint: [brief | site | redesign <url|dir> | component | resume | status | jury | ship] [target] [--quick] [--gsap|--shader|--3d] [--no-found-pictures|--found-pictures]
refuse: Writing page code before the direction contract is locked, or choosing the stack before the concept: both throw work away.
Fade-and-rise on every section, parallax on everything, bounce or elastic easing by reflex: motion as wallpaper.
Hero-metric rows, identical feature-card grids, eyebrows, numbered markers by habit, the hero → logos → features → testimonials → pricing order: the template a juror recognises first.
"Get started", "Learn more", "Discover" as actions: a conversion that names no outcome.
Inter, Space Grotesk, DM Sans, Manrope, Geist or a system face as the display voice: the generator's signature.
Dark + neon + glow, gradient text, glass by default, a blob or particle hero: the Awwwards default, refused in THESIS.
A blocking preloader with no concept, or one that plays in full on every visit: the load gate that costs usability.
WebGL because it is expected: every rung of dosage costs a pipeline, a tier system and a mirror; take it only when a beat needs depth.
A global `animation: none` as the reduced-motion path; hover-only or drag-only affordances; canvas text with no DOM mirror.
Silently skipping the jury, softening its disposition, or shipping with the audit red and no exception recorded.
Reusing a reference's section order, copy, hexes, pairing or assets, whatever the user's shorthand seems to ask for; the corpus gives principles, the DIVERGENCE block records the refusals.

skills.short: Finds the one idea, the story and the signature; deals three directions and writes the direction contract.
skills.title: the direction contract
skills.description: Find the concept for an award-worthy site or component before any code: the one idea the page owns, its scroll story, the signature interaction and a committed visual world, diverging from a corpus of analysed award winners. Use when the user asks for ideas, creative direction, a 'big idea', storytelling or scrollytelling, 'how would an award-winning studio approach this', 'what would make this site win', or when a build has no direction yet. Deals three directions and a conventional exit with a seeded roll, locks one in a single question and writes the AWARDS.md contract. Never copies a reference site. Not for copywriting alone, dashboards or feature work.
skills.lead: Find the concept for an award-worthy site or component before any code: the one idea the page owns, its scroll story, the signature interaction and a committed visual world, diverging from a corpus of analysed award winners.
skills.intro: This skill produces the one artefact every later phase depends on: a direction contract in `AWARDS.md` whose blocks are concrete enough to build from and specific enough that no juror can trace the page to a reference site. It reads the corpus, diverges from it, deals candidate worlds with a seeded roll, lets the user lock one, and writes the contract.
sections: Step 1 — the inventory, the scene and the four ruts
Step 2 — corpus neighbours and the DIVERGENCE block
refuse: Mood adjectives as concepts (premium, immersive, bold, cinematic, clean): they fail the memory test by definition.
Effect as concept ("a WebGL hero with distortion", "particles that react to the cursor"): an effect is a technique tier, and a technique is not an idea.

The category rut, the Awwwards rut, the template skeleton and the plugin rut, however the user phrases the request; all four are named in THESIS as refusals, written for this subject rather than copied from the template.
An idea that still works with the nearest competitor's name in it, a world tagged with no engine, seven worlds on fewer than four engines, and stimuli dealt after the worlds were written.
Code-only imagery chosen before the open collections were searched while found pictures are on, and the corpus's modal colour strategy taken without a deal or a reason.
Any card's signature, section order, copy, palette, type pairing or asset, including when the user asks for "something like" a named site; the card's principle is offered instead.

A direction that needs assets the user cannot supply (a commissioned object per variant, drone footage, a full bake pipeline) unless the brief labels them synthetic and they can be authored for the build.

A deal without the script, an undealt world locked or offered, three variants of one idea presented as three worlds, any option beyond the dealt cards, the exit and re-roll, more than two re-rolls, a second question round.
A gate in front of the content, two interruptions, two signatures, or a scroll model chosen for spectacle rather than for the story.
Faces, hexes or effect parameters written into WORLD: that is `awards:system` and `awards:motion` work, done with the reference files they own.

skills.short: The type contract, the colour strategy and the tokens; writes DESIGN.md and tokens.css.
skills.title: the visual system
skills.description: Turn a direction into the visual system of an award-level site and write DESIGN.md plus tokens.css: a typeface contract, a fluid type scale locked to an artboard, two to four colour tokens under a named strategy, spacing, grid, radius and shadow policy, section themes, easing tokens and themed browser surfaces. Use when the user asks for design tokens, a palette, fonts or typography, 'pick fonts and colours for …', a design system, DESIGN.md, 'make the type feel premium', theme switching, or when an awards build has no DESIGN.md yet. Avoids the reflex faces and generated palettes. Not for Tailwind conversions, Figma hand-offs or styling without award framing.
skills.lead: Turn a direction into the visual system of an award-level site and write DESIGN.md plus tokens.css: a typeface contract, a fluid type scale locked to an artboard, two to four colour tokens under a named strategy, spacing, grid, radius and shadow policy, section themes, easing tokens and themed browser surfaces.
skills.intro: This skill turns the WORLD block of a direction contract into the tokens every later phase builds with: one type contract, two to four colour tokens under a named strategy, a spacing base, a material policy, motion tokens and themed browser surfaces. It writes `DESIGN.md` and `src/styles/tokens.css`, keeps their values identical, and proves the result with the audit.
refuse: A generated six-hue palette, the indigo-violet pair, teal + orange, pastel rainbow, gold on black: a wheel, not a world.
Gradient text, glass panels by default, glow as a default register, hard offset shadows outside a deliberate neobrutalist world: costume, not material.
A Google Fonts or any CDN `<link>`, more than four font files, a display face that swaps late and shreds split lines.
A system face or a reflex-list face as the display voice by habit; two display faces; a third layer without a hundred items to organise.
Pure #000 under pure #FFF with no diegetic reason and no exception; a dark ground chosen because award sites "are dark".
Theme by habit: a dark mode nobody asked the use scene for, or a theme that fails contrast because "it is only one section".
A second accent as a token; an accent used as body text; tracking tighter than −0.06em; display type above 13 vw or without a `clamp()`.

Any corpus card's set or pairing as a package (bone + near-black, the five jewellery tokens, the four portfolio themes, the six flavour hues, silver + flare red, the named face pairings in `typography.md`).
Values in `DESIGN.md` that differ from `tokens.css`, or token names that differ from the shared recipe names.

skills.short: The page map, the hero archetype, the components and the semantic skeleton, 404 included.
skills.title: page map and skeleton
skills.description: Plan and build the page architecture of an award-level site: the chapter or route map and its pacing, the hero archetype, navigation and menu overlay, preloader slot, pinned stacks, horizontal rails, galleries, archive lists, a designed footer and 404, as semantic HTML with keyboard paths and a responsive plan. Use when the user asks for page structure, sections, 'what sections should this have', wireframes, a landing-page or portfolio layout, a hero that 'needs to feel premium', a nav, menu, footer or 404, scrollytelling structure, or to turn a locked direction into markup. Not for dashboards, admin CRUD, forms-only pages or accessibility fixes without award framing.
skills.lead: Plan and build the page architecture of an award-level site: the chapter or route map and its pacing, the hero archetype, navigation and menu overlay, preloader slot, pinned stacks, horizontal rails, galleries, archive lists, a designed footer and 404, as semantic HTML with keyboard paths and a responsive plan.
skills.intro: This skill turns a locked direction into the architecture of the page: a page map with beats and pacing, one hero archetype, the components each chapter needs, a semantic DOM plan, a responsive strategy decided before any component exists, and the static skeleton itself, 404 included. Motion and WebGL come later and must survive on top of what this phase ships.
sections: Step 6 — the responsive strategy, decided before build
refuse: The hero-metric template, eyebrow labels and pills over headings, meaningless section numbering, identical card grids and icon tiles, cards inside cards, repeated "Not X. A Y." slogans, promise words and a dash in every sentence: the slop families the audit catches (L04, L05, X07, X08, X16–X18, X20) and a juror recognises first. The rest of the scan is in `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/references/anti-patterns.md#the-slop-scan`.
The features → testimonials → pricing order unless the story earned it; a chapter that exists because the category always has one.
A modal by reflex; an overlay hidden with opacity that stays focusable; a menu with no `inert`, trap or Escape.
Two hero archetypes stacked; a hero that needs the paragraph to make sense; a card's signature as drawn.
A chapter with nothing to read; two interruptions; a gate in front of the content; a marquee as the hero.
Canvas-only text or images; a click handler on a `div`; hover-only previews; drag-only galleries.
Two scaling systems on one page; a reload at a breakpoint; a rotate-your-device prompt; a mobile version that drops headings, copy or links.
The host's default 404; a sitemap dump or a social-icon row as the ending.
Content that only appears once JavaScript runs; a preloader element that hides the page without a script.
Any card's section order or component lifted with its values, whatever the user's shorthand names.

skills.short: Scaffolds Vite, Next, Nuxt, Astro or SvelteKit with Lenis and GSAP on one ticker.
skills.description: Choose, scaffold and boot the technical foundation of a creative-developer site: Vite + vanilla by default, or Next.js, Nuxt, Astro, SvelteKit + Threlte or a Webflow shell. Wires Lenis and GSAP ScrollTrigger on one ticker, lazy-chunks Three.js, self-hosts fonts, picks the page-transition mechanism, the glTF/Draco/KTX2 pipeline, quality tiers and one reduced-motion switch. Use when asked to set up, scaffold or configure a project for smooth scroll, GSAP, Lenis, Three.js, WebGL or page transitions, which framework suits an award-style site, or to add these to an existing Next, Nuxt, Astro, Svelte or Webflow app. Not for CRUD or dashboard scaffolds, nor for authoring animations (awards:motion).
skills.lead: Choose, scaffold and boot the technical foundation of a creative-developer site: Vite + vanilla by default, or Next.js, Nuxt, Astro, SvelteKit + Threlte or a Webflow shell.
skills.intro: Pick the stack, scaffold it, and boot Lenis, GSAP and (when the concept needs it) Three on one clock, so every later phase inherits a page that scrolls, measures and degrades correctly. The stack is a decision made once per project; the architecture under it is the same on every stack in the corpus.
sections: The stack is a decision, the architecture is the constant
refuse: Two smooth-scroll libraries (Lenis beside ScrollSmoother, Locomotive or `ScrollTrigger.normalizeScroll(true)`): two scroll positions that disagree every frame. Locomotive 5 also bundles its own older Lenis (`stacks/locomotive-scroll-5.0.md`).
CSS `scroll-behavior: smooth` beside Lenis: `scrollTo` fights the browser and the audit flags it [M05].
A Google Fonts CDN link or a foundry `@import`: a third-party request before first paint and an audit failure [T02].
A `position: fixed` canvas whose planes drift against their placeholders: fix the clock (absolute re-offset or a scroll uniform), never the scroll.
Framer Motion or `motion` for scroll scrub: no winner shipped it; scrubbed timelines are ScrollTrigger with `ease: 'none'` (`stacks/motion-13.4.md` names what Motion is for).
A canvas per page, or two WebGL contexts on one page: resources cannot be shared and the second context is the one that gets lost.
`location.reload()` at a breakpoint, or two scores toggled with `display: none`: focus, scroll position and every live region are lost mid-visit.
`ssr: false`, `client:only` or an empty shell to dodge `window` errors: it deletes the DOM mirror the accessibility score is made of.
Bumping a pinned version because a newer one exists: bump one library at a time and re-run the recipe verification.

Tailwind or a component library added by reflex. Winners do ship Tailwind, but as their own token layer (`[site:usavionix]` v4 tokens, `[site:shopify-editions-w26]` an oklch palette), never as the stock look; use it where the project already does, wired to the DESIGN.md tokens.
Scaffolding into a non-empty directory, or a scaffold whose placeholders ship.

skills.description: Author the motion of an award-level site or component with GSAP 3.15 (ScrollTrigger, SplitText, Flip), Lenis, anime.js 4 or CSS: preloaders on a real load signal, masked reveals, scrubbed pins and sticky stages, velocity effects, cursors, magnetic targets, marquees, page transitions, one easing vocabulary and three reduced-motion tiers. Use when asked to animate, add motion or smooth scroll, build GSAP timelines or scrollytelling, text reveals, transitions, micro-interactions or cursor effects, make a page feel alive, premium or cinematic, or fix motion that feels generic, janky or fade-up-everything. Not for chart animation or the WebGL layer (awards:webgl).
skills.lead: Author the motion of an award-level site or component with GSAP 3.15 (ScrollTrigger, SplitText, Flip), Lenis, anime.js 4 or CSS: preloaders on a real load signal, masked reveals, scrubbed pins and sticky stages, velocity effects, cursors, magnetic targets, marquees, page transitions, one easing vocabulary and three reduced-motion tiers.
skills.intro: Write the motion score first, then build it: one authored moment per chapter, one signature, one easing family, one clock, and a reduced-motion tier that still shows every state. Motion is the layer a jury feels before it can name it, and it is where "generic" gets diagnosed.
sections: Where the score lives per stack
refuse: Fade-and-rise on every section at 400 ms on the default ease: the tell that motion was applied, not authored.
Bounce, elastic or back easing on UI feedback: it belongs to one landing the story earns.
Parallax on everything: depth with no beat behind it.
Scroll-jacking with no keyboard exit, or a virtual float on a page that is a document.
A blocking preloader with no concept, no skip, or a timer for a signal; one that replays in full on every visit.
Hover-only affordances, drag-only galleries, a cursor with no coarse-pointer guard.
Animating layout properties; `will-change` on `*`; a second ticker; raw wheel deltas as an effect input; 60 fps constants shipped untransformed.
Eased scrubs that fight the scroll; `pin: true` where a sticky stage works.
A global animation kill presented as the reduced-motion path; marquees and flickers that keep running under it.
Framer Motion or `motion` for scroll scrub; two smooth-scroll libraries.

`[clone:floema-jewelry]`'s bulge and flight, `[site:leo-parpeix]`'s cursor badges and counter jumps, `[site:the-line]`'s hinge and `00/24` leader, or any corpus device reproduced as a signature: they are pattern pointers, never parts.

skills.short: The GL layer in Three.js, OGL or React Three Fiber, with quality tiers and a page that works without it.
skills.description: Build the WebGL layer of an award-level site with Three.js 0.186, OGL, React Three Fiber or Threlte: DOM-tethered image planes, fluid and distortion post-processing, depth-map parallax, scroll-driven camera rigs, render-to-texture transitions, one hero object, particles, the glTF + Draco + KTX2 pipeline, quality tiers, disposal, a DOM mirror and a no-GL fallback. Use when asked for 3D, WebGL, a Three.js or R3F scene, shaders or GLSL, particles, liquid, fluid or distortion effects, a 3D hero or scroll-scrubbed models, and when a canvas site is slow, drifts against the DOM or renders dark. Not for DOM-only motion (awards:motion), charts, or 'make it 3D' with no concept behind it.
skills.lead: Build the WebGL layer of an award-level site with Three.js 0.186, OGL, React Three Fiber or Threlte: DOM-tethered image planes, fluid and distortion post-processing, depth-map parallax, scroll-driven camera rigs, render-to-texture transitions, one hero object, particles, the glTF + Draco + KTX2 pipeline, quality tiers, disposal, a DOM mirror and a no-GL fallback.
skills.intro: Fix the dose before the first mesh, let the DOM own layout, feed scroll and pointer to the shaders as numbers, and ship a page that still reads with the context blocked. WebGL earns a Developer Award when it disappears into the page; it loses one when the page disappears into it.
sections: Quality tiers and the three-tier fallback
refuse: A blob, particle field or floating primitives with no beat behind them; "make it 3D" as a brief: a concept, not a shader, is missing.
Text or images that exist only in the canvas: the accessibility score and find-in-page are made of the DOM.
An uncapped `devicePixelRatio`, or a 3× phone rendering bloom at full resolution: the classic 12 fps site.
A 50 MB glb, a PNG into a shader, a decoder pulled from a CDN at runtime: the pipeline exists to prevent all three.
Two contexts on one page, a canvas per section, a scene that outlives its route.
Scroll or pointer written to framework state; raw wheel deltas as uniforms.
Per-scene bloom values chosen by eye; both post pipelines at once.
A canvas with no fallback: no static tier, no text tier, no `--no-webgl` capture.
Runtime simulation of anything the visitor cannot influence: bake it.
The Floema bulge, the Léo Parpeix wake, the Igloo ice, the Mont-fort peak, the Lando visor, the Shopify paintings or the Slosh can shipped as the signature: pattern pointers, never parts.

Use when the user wants a specific element 'award-worthy', 'award-level', 'more premium / memorable', a menu, cursor or marquee 'like the creative studios do', or one section with real motion without redesigning the site. Inherits the site's tokens, adds one signature interaction with every state, keyboard, touch and reduced-motion path, and verifies it in a capture. Not for whole sites (awards:craft), dashboards, admin UI or bug fixes.
skills.lead: Design and build ONE award-worthy component in an existing site or standalone: a hero, preloader, nav overlay, cursor, marquee, sticky stack, gallery, hover list, page transition, footer or 404.
skills.intro: The fast path. A component inside an established world inherits that world; it is never a new identity exercise. The job is to give one element a signature move, every state and every path, and to prove it with a capture, while touching nothing around it.
refuse: Restyling anything outside the named target; the surrounding page is the given.
A second font family, a new palette or a new dependency for one component; if the world genuinely lacks a primitive, say which and ask.
Hover-only affordances, drag-only galleries, effects with no state and no keyboard path.
Pasting a recipe unchanged, demo copy and demo tokens included.
WebGL, particles or a cursor trail because they are expected; the mini contract's SIGNATURE line decides.
"Make it premium" answered with glow, gradient text or glass: those are the reflex families in `anti-patterns.md`.

skills.short: Scores the page from screenshots in a fresh context, then returns ordered fixes and one word.
skills.title: the fresh-context jury
skills.description: Scores a site, page or component the way a design-award jury does: Design, Usability, Creativity and Content on anchored scales, the six Developer Award criteria, the memory and specificity tests, a keyboard and reduced-motion walk and a slop scan, ending in ordered fixes and one disposition (ship, fix, rebuild or recapture). Use when the user asks to review, critique, score, judge, rate or evaluate a site or component, asks 'would this win', 'is this award-worthy', 'what is missing', 'what would the jury say', says an award-level page looks generic, templated or AI-made, or before shipping award-level work; --verdict re-checks a fix batch. Runs in a fresh context on captures and the audit. Not for code review, failing tests or accessibility work without award framing.
skills.lead: Scores a site, page or component the way a design-award jury does: Design, Usability, Creativity and Content on anchored scales, the six Developer Award criteria, the memory and specificity tests, a keyboard and reduced-motion walk and a slop scan, ending in ordered fixes and one disposition (ship, fix, rebuild or recapture).
skills.intro: Read `AWARDS.md` and `DESIGN.md` in the project root when they exist; `## Status` in `AWARDS.md` says which phases are done, so resume from there instead of restarting. Read impeccable's `PRODUCT.md` for product truth when it exists and never overwrite it. Detect the scope (a whole site, one component named by file or selector, or a critique of something that already exists) and the stack (framework, animation and 3D libraries, build tool) from `package.json`, lockfiles and the entry files. When the request is clearly a whole site and no direction contract exists yet, offer `/awards:craft` once, then proceed with this skill.
refuse: Praise, softening, or any score without a reason next to it.
Redesigning inside the report: name the fix and its location; `awards:ship` makes it.
Scoring without valid captures, or from the source alone.
Counting effects as creativity, or accepting a mood as a memory-test answer.
Letting the contract, the motion score or the build's commit messages argue a score upward.
Editing anything in the project beyond the report file and the log lines.

skills.short: Applies the fixes in one batch, then runs the audit, captures, budgets and meta checks.
skills.title: fix, prove, report
skills.description: Takes an award-level site or component from 'it works' to 'it ships': applies the jury's fixes in one batch, runs the craft-floor audit until every finding is fixed or excepted, captures every viewport and state, checks the performance budgets (JS, GL chunk, images, fonts, LCP, CLS), meta, Open Graph, favicon and 404, and writes the ship report. Use when the user says ship, launch, finalize, polish, QA, 'production-ready', 'check performance or accessibility', 'run the audit', 'take screenshots', or after any awards build or jury round in a project with an AWARDS.md. Not a deploy tool, nor for app screens without award framing.
skills.lead: Takes an award-level site or component from 'it works' to 'it ships': applies the jury's fixes in one batch, runs the craft-floor audit until every finding is fixed or excepted, captures every viewport and state, checks the performance budgets (JS, GL chunk, images, fonts, LCP, CLS), meta, Open Graph, favicon and 404, and writes the ship report.
skills.intro: The jury judges; this skill fixes and proves. A ship pass ends with evidence a stranger could check: an audit at zero, manifest-derived valid captures, measured budgets and a report. It never redesigns, because a fix that needs a new idea is a concept problem and goes back to `awards:craft`.
refuse: A reduced-motion branch that kills everything (`* { animation: none !important }` or a global 0.01 ms duration); tier the motion instead (M02).
Removing the signature to pass a budget; tier it, lazy-load it or lower its resolution.
A preloader that runs longer than 2.5 s on a repeat visit, or one not tied to a real load signal.
Excepting a P0 finding, or any finding without a reason a juror would accept.
Redesigning during the fix batch, or adding fixes the jury did not list.
Writing "shipped" with the audit red, a capture unopened or a budget unmeasured.

skills.title: turn a site into a case study
skills.description: Turns a reference website into a case-study card in the awards corpus format: concept, palette, type, components, motion parameters, stack evidence, weaknesses, principles and take / don't take, every claim labelled by confidence. Captures with Playwright and inspects source when the site's owner allows it, and records recalled material honestly when not. Use when the user shares a site to learn from, asks 'what makes this site award-winning', 'analyse / deconstruct / break down this site', 'why did this win', 'add this to the references', or pastes a CSSDA, FWA or other award-gallery entry. Not for SEO or content audits, nor for downloading a site's assets.
skills.lead: Turns a reference website into a case-study card in the awards corpus format: concept, palette, type, components, motion parameters, stack evidence, weaknesses, principles and take / don't take, every claim labelled by confidence.
skills.intro: Read `AWARDS.md` and `DESIGN.md` in the project root when they exist; `## Status` in `AWARDS.md` says which phases are done, so resume from there instead of restarting. Read impeccable's `PRODUCT.md` for product truth when it exists and never overwrite it. Detect the scope (a whole site, one component named by file or selector, or a critique of something that already exists) and the stack (framework, animation and 3D libraries, build tool) from `package.json`, lockfiles and the entry files. When the request is clearly a whole site and no direction contract exists yet, offer `/awards:craft` once, then proceed with this skill.
sections: The corpus is the skill's taste
refuse: Scraping: crawling routes, bulk downloads, saving images, fonts, videos, audio or 3D models, or working around a block.
Reproduction: rebuilding the site, or carrying its copy, palette hexes, section order or signature into a new build.
Unevidenced stack claims: naming a library, a CMS or a studio without a signature or a label.
Inventing awards, scores, dates or credits; upgrading a `[recalled]` claim because it sounds right.
Quoting more than 25 words of the site's copy, or pasting its copy into the card as description.

axes.measures: Whether the page owns a visual world: type, colour, space, imagery and chrome as one system, and whether the first viewport is unforgettable
Whether every visitor can reach the content and the conversion: wayfinding, load, keyboard, touch, reduced motion, mobile
Whether one concept does the work a feature list usually does, and whether the medium enacts it
Whether the copy and assets are specific, true and authored at full fidelity

developer.name: Semantics / SEO
developer.high: A descriptive title and meta description per page, canonical and Open Graph text, one h1 and an unbroken outline, landmarks, `lang`, and every word a canvas draws also present in the DOM
developer.mid: Present but generic: one title for every route, no description
developer.low: No title, headings chosen by size, an empty DOM behind a canvas

developer.name: Animations / Transitions
developer.high: One ticker, framerate-independent damping, scrubbed tweens with `ease:'none'`, velocity as input, every loop paused off-screen
developer.mid: Smooth but some jank on resize or route change
developer.low: Layout-property animation, dropped frames, scroll-jack with no exit

developer.name: Accessibility
developer.high: Every text at 4.5:1 (large 3:1) in every state including focus, a focus ring at 3:1, keyboard for every gesture, a skip link, targets ≥ 24 px (44 px for the top band), alt text, reduced-motion tiers, no axe-core violations
developer.mid: Partial: some labels, some focus styles, a contrast slip

developer.name: WPO
developer.high: Entry JS ≤ 200 KB gz, GL in its own lazy chunk, compressed textures and meshes, LCP ≤ 2.5 s throttled
developer.mid: One heavy asset or an uncapped DPR
developer.low: Multi-megabyte rasters, blocking fonts, no code splitting

developer.name: Responsive Design
developer.high: Strategy decided (vw-lock or breakpoints), coarse-pointer swaps, no overflow, touch targets ≥ 44 px
developer.low: Desktop only; a reload at a breakpoint

developer.name: Markup / Meta-data
developer.high: Valid, semantic markup with unique ids, theme-color, colour-scheme, favicon and Open Graph image, no console errors, disposal on route change, no debug flags shipped
developer.low: Errors, duplicate ids or tickers, leaked renderers

raise.do: Decide the colour strategy; hold one type contract; author load, close, 404 and browser surfaces; give the page pacing
raise.not: Add effects, add a font, add a gradient

raise.do: Run the walk; add keyboard paths; skip the preloader on repeat; collapse eccentric nav on touch; ship reduced-motion tiers
Make the signature enact the thesis; make one metaphor do two jobs; cut every effect that does not serve it
Replace adjectives with numbers; separate registers by chapter; label synthetic assets

honest: Score from the captures and the audit before reading the direction contract, so the contract cannot argue you upward.
Write the one-line reason next to each score. A score without a reason is a feeling.
Compare against the exemplars above. If you give a Design 9, name the corpus site it would beat.
Never round a middling axis up because another axis is strong. The weighted score exists to do that arithmetic.
Scores drive the disposition (`report-template.md`); the disposition drives the fix list. Praise is not part of the output.

dispositions.rule: weighted 7.2 or higher, no axis below 6.8, no P0/P1 findings, every contract row kept, usability walk steps 1 and 3 passed.
the weighted score is 6.8 to 7.19, or any axis is below 6.8, or the audit has P0/P1 findings, or a contract block is not kept.

the weighted score is below 6.8, or a juror could name the source site from the first viewport, or the memory test yields a mood instead of an object or a behaviour, or the THESIS is not visible in the first viewport.
the evidence is invalid or could not be produced: a capture missing, blank, stale, showing a stuck preloader, or page errors that prevented rendering.

jury.caps: A named source site or a nameable generator (two or more slop-scan families) caps Creativity at 6, effects with no concept cap Creativity at 6, failed walk steps cap Usability as the walk states.

phases.name: Brief
phases.does: At most three questions: what only this subject can prove, who reads it and where, and what a visitor should do.
phases.quote: a €12 timed viewing of the drawer room (six people, twenty minutes, Tuesday to Sunday). The action is "Book a viewing, €12" …

phases.name: Concept
phases.does: Seven candidate worlds, three dealt by a seeded roll, one locked and written down as a direction contract.
phases.quote: The page is a paint cross-section under the museum's microscope: a sliver of seven paint layers set in a resin block …

phases.name: System
phases.does: One type contract, two to four colour tokens under a named strategy, self-hosted faces, every browser surface themed.
phases.quote: restrained duotone with chroma from the specimen only. A cool off-white ground (the light of a microscope's field) and a near-black ink carry every word …

phases.name: Structure
phases.does: Chapters with beats, one interruption and a designed close, as semantic HTML before any motion. The hero is built and judged first.
phases.quote: 7 rows, the 404 among them: The block (hero) · Used up and taken, 1964 · 1943 · Unbearable and poisonous …

phases.name: Stack
phases.does: Vite by default; Lenis and GSAP on one ticker, and a hook that lets captures drive the page.
phases.quote: Vite 8.3 + vanilla JS, MPA (index and 404), relative base; GSAP 3.15 and Lenis 1.3 on GSAP's ticker …

phases.name: Motion
phases.does: One authored moment per chapter, each with a reduced-motion tier, never a global animation kill.
phases.quote: 9 rows. Signature: the microscope descends: scroll, continuous from the block's exit to the drawer room

phases.name: WebGL
phases.does: Only where a beat needs depth: its own lazy chunk, a DOM mirror, and a page that works without it.
phases.file: the GL chunk, or a written decline
phases.quote: GL chunk: 4.8 KB for the field module (the shader and its WebGL2 setup) plus 0.3 KB of pigment data, lazy …

phases.name: Jury
phases.does: A juror in a separate session reads the captures before the contract, scores four axes and ends on one word.
phases.quote: 2026-10-23 · component .chapter--block · rebuild · D 7.3 / U 5.5 / C 7.2 → mean 6.67

phases.name: Ship
phases.does: The fixes in one batch, the audit clean or every exception explained, the performance measured.
phases.quote: 2026-10-23 · audit P0 0 / P1 0 / P2 0 / P3 0 · exceptions 1 · captures 5 valid · entry 52.8 KB …

lines.text: WebGL layer built or explicitly declined (webgl)

contract.rule: the one idea this surface owns, built on an inventory item; the category default, the Awwwards default, the template skeleton and the plugin's own latest default (`references/patterns/house-tells.md`) it refuses, each as it would look for this subject; then `Competitor test: <nearest competitor> — <why the thesis breaks for it>`.

colour strategy (dealt with `roll.mjs --choose`, with the reason it fits) and tokens, type contract, materials, and one imagery strategy with what supplies it (owned photographs; with none, real pictures of the subject's world from a named open collection before a generation tool, a drawn language or code, unless `Found pictures: off`) — recognisable with every word removed. "None, flat grounds" is not a strategy.
the narrative model, the chapter beats (entrance · hold · exit), the interruption, the close.
the exact composition — what is where, at what scale, and where the primary action sits.
the one interaction, the physical metaphor it enacts and the jobs it does, its technique tier, its behaviour on touch, keyboard and reduced motion, its fallback.
native + Lenis / sticky stages + invisible rails / virtual float / section switcher — and why this story needs it.
what the preloader does and its real load signal; what the last screen is.
the three nearest corpus cards as `[site:slug]`; the principle taken from each; the literal move refused from each.
unreviewed and unshipped is unfinished — this build ends with a jury disposition and a ship report.

scripts.what: Checks Node, npm, the dependencies, Playwright and an actual browser launch before a build. Installs nothing and changes no configuration; exit 2 names what is missing.
Copies a scaffold with one ticker and the capture hook already wired.
The seeded roll the concept skill deals directions, outside stimuli, colour strategies and hero archetypes with.
Faces chosen by character from the open Fontsource catalogue: a seeded pull, a rendered specimen of your own headline, then the files and their licence.
DESIGN.md through Google’s design.md tools: lint it, export its tokens, or diff them between rounds.
Real pictures from open collections (public domain, CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA only) and the project’s asset and licence log.
The craft-floor audit: rules in eight families, static by default; --render opens the page at desktop, tablet and phone widths.
Jury evidence: scroll positions at three widths, accessibility trees, reduced motion, scripted states and a keyboard walk; timelines, video and throttled passes on request.
The composition block map and measured fingerprint of one page.
Chrome UX Report field data (p75) for a live site. Needs CRUX_API_KEY.
What the plugin’s own finished builds share, so a new contract can refuse the plugin’s own rut.
Builds every recipe and drives its verifier in headless Chromium with WebGL.
Manifest versions, pins against versions.md, shared copies, licence files and every count the descriptions quote.
Every pinned library against the npm registry’s latest, without installing anything.
The score figures the rubric quotes, recomputed from the site cards.
Every [site:], [recipe:] and [pattern:] reference resolves to a real file.

hooks.what: After a compaction, re-attaches a short state card from an unfinished build’s AWARDS.md: phase, next skill, deep modes, last jury and ship lines.
Adds one routing line when a prompt carries explicit award framing; a hint, never a gate.
Runs the quick audit on the file just edited or written. Silent unless the project has an AWARDS.md.
Sends the juror’s reply back once when it lacks its literal disposition line, which craft routes on.
